markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **support-weighted history pooling with multi-negative training**: a small SASRec extension targeting isolated-purchase overreaction, broad recommendations, and weak lower-tail ranking margins. Improvements remain hypotheses until measured under the pinned evaluator.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already captures recent context. A pooled history residual can test whether repeated interests deserve additional weight. (2) Users report broad relevance and overreaction to occasional purchases. Recurrence-weighted historical evidence directly targets these two failures without claiming to infer equipment ownership. (3) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin. These training diagnostics motivate stronger discrimination, but do not establish validation performance or severe embedding collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [IBLSRec](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10820829/) distinguishes stable relationships from transient associations. This motivates testing separate persistent and recent signals. (2) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) supports multiple negatives and calibrated BCE. It provides a practical objective alternative without extra metadata. (3) [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) identifies instability and false-negative risks from aggressive mining. Uniform negatives are therefore the appropriate first experiment.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Organize changes along evidence aggregation, ranking discrimination, and negative difficulty. Scores below are Originality / Potential / User alignment / Model alignment / Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive / negative assessment for each axis |
|---|---|---|
| A: Support-weighted pooling + gBCE | 5/7/8/8/4 | O: targeted combination / familiar components; P: reusable residual / may oversmooth; U: reinforces recurring intent / cannot establish compatibility; M: strengthens separation / margins may mislead; D: small extension / prefix masking needs care |
| B: Training-transition graph residual | 5/6/6/6/6 | O: directional evidence / established graph approach; P: sparse associations / rare transitions; U: concrete behavioral links / associations lack purpose; M: adds ranking evidence / noisy edges; D: sparse implementation / predictor integration |
| C: Warmed-up stochastic hard negatives | 3/7/4/9/4 | O: established recipe / little novelty; P: targeted discrimination / false negatives; U: removes confusing candidates / weak preference support; M: targets lower tail / training overfit; D: unchanged inference / sampling overhead |

**Selected algorithm: A.** For each causal prefix, pool item embeddings with weights combining recency and similarity support from other prefix items. Learn a scalar residual gate and score candidates with the resulting feature. Repeated coherent interests receive more support than isolated purchases, addressing broad relevance and occasional-purchase overreaction; multi-negative gBCE targets weak separation. Similarity is only a preference proxy, not proof of functional compatibility or satisfied needs.

**Implementation and evaluation.** Start with pooling-only and gBCE-only ablations, then combine them. Preserve all four datasets, seeds, routing, diagnostic adapter, and predictor writer. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; report category results and lower-tail margins separately. No experiments or gains are claimed.

idea.description: Extend per-dataset SASRec with a causal, support-weighted history residual and multi-negative generalized BCE. Repeated, coherent historical interests strengthen the sequence representation, while the objective improves discrimination against multiple sampled alternatives.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies overly broad recommendations and excessive influence from occasional purchases. A support-weighted residual explicitly targets both. Electronics also exhibits weak lower-tail training separation, motivating a multi-negative objective. Neither mechanism establishes compatibility, ownership, or whether a need has been satisfied.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, and the existing SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with default 200. Compute support causally from normalized prefix item embeddings, using detached similarities and excluding padding and self-similarity. Use bounded positive weights, a learned sigmoid scalar residual gate initialized near zero, and trainable pooling projection. Start with 128 uniform negatives and gBCE calibration t=0.75; exclude the current positive and observed training-history items, without consulting validation or test labels. Implement gBCE using its published sampling correction and stable log-space arithmetic. Compare baseline, pooling-only, gBCE-only, and combined configurations within the remaining shared budget. Save architecture configuration and parameters beneath the trial directory, and update the predictor writer to reconstruct the same model. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. The view must expose the actual model, its item embeddings, augmented log2feats, consistent predict_score, and permitted history/metadata. Remove unavailable category breakdowns or explicitly mark them unavailable; do not fabricate review fields. Tune exclusively with the pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
class SupportedSASRec:
    log2feats(sequence):
        h = sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
        e = item_emb(sequence)
        z = normalize(e.detach(), dim=-1)
        for each valid position t:
            prefix = valid_positions_up_to(t)
            sim = z[prefix] @ z[prefix].T
            support[j] = mean(relu(sim[j, k]) for k != j)
            # Singleton support is zero; all operations exclude padding.
            weight[j] = exp(-decay * (t-j)) * (1 + support[j])
            pooled = sum(weight[j] * e[j]) / sum(weight)
            output[t] = h[t] + sigmoid(gate) * projection(pooled)
        return output

for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = SupportedSASRec(dataset)
    for epoch in configured_epochs:
        for _, sequence, positive, _ in train_loader:
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            negatives = sample_uniform_unseen_training_items(K=128)
            loss = published_stable_gBCE(
                score(features, positive),
                score(features, negatives),
                calibration_t=0.75,
                catalog_size=dataset.item_count)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
    save_model_configuration_and_weights_under_trial_directory()
write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_dataset_routing()
select_configuration_by_pinned_macro_validation_HR_at_10()

originality.positive: Connects recurrence support, a gated SASRec residual, and calibrated multi-negative learning to specific observed failures.
originality.negative: Pooling, residual gates, and generalized BCE are established components; novelty lies primarily in their targeted combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides a small, ablatable foundation for separating persistent preference support from recent context.
future_potential.negative: Embedding similarity may reproduce broad associations, and pooling can obscure multiple distinct interests.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains SASRec, item-dot-product scoring, and the existing dataset routes; inference requires only a pooled residual.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal support weighting, stable gBCE, negative exclusions, and synchronized predictor serialization require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces causal self-attention over interaction histories for next-item recommendation.
limitations: The supplied diagnosis shows that this baseline can overemphasize broad associations and has uneven training-pair separation across the four datasets.

related_work.title: IBLSRec
contributions: Distinguishes stable item relationships from short-lived associations and uses latent intent to refine preferences, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluation.

related_work.title: gSASRec: IJCAI 2024 summary
contributions: Combines multiple negatives with generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: Its published findings do not establish improvements for this exact four-category, 99-negative benchmark.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Uses warm-start training, progressive negative difficulty, and stochastic selection to moderate hard-negative mining.
limitations: Mining adds training cost and retains false-negative risk.
